title: Sampling and Representation
outcome: By the end, I can define a population, selection frame and nonresponse report for a survey.
scenario: A fictional Grade 7 class wants to understand book-format preferences across its whole grade.
given: Population: all 60 Grade 7 learners. Frame: current school-approved list of those 60, used only by the teacher.
Teacher randomly invites 15; 12 answer the same neutral comic/prose/either question. No names enter the analysis table.

steps.label: Define target
steps.detail: The question concerns all Grade 7, not only library-club members.

steps.label: Select invitations
steps.detail: Teacher uses the complete approved list and documented random selection.

steps.label: Record responses
steps.detail: 12 replies from 15 invited; three nonresponses remain visible.

steps.label: Report scope
steps.detail: Invitation response rate 12/15=80%; preference counts describe respondents.

explanation: A sample plan states who could be selected, how selection happens and what happens after invitation. Random invitations do not guarantee that respondents resemble those who declined. Use a neutral question and preserve nonresponse coverage. Learners can discuss aggregate counts without receiving the identifiable selection frame.

counterfactual.change: Invite only the 15 library-club members instead.
counterfactual.prediction: The invitation process no longer covers the whole grade through this frame.
counterfactual.reason: Club members may differ in reading interests; selection is now limited to one group.

student_task: Can 80% response be reported as 80% of the whole grade responding?
teacher_answer: No. Twelve of fifteen invited is 80%; twelve of sixty in the grade is 20%. Denominators answer different questions.
project_evidence: Document whose requests inform the recommender and avoid treating an easily reached group as all intended users.
limits: Even the random-invitation plan does not remove nonresponse bias or justify revealing identifiable school lists.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
